evals.prompt: We use Azure DevOps Services. Protect main with a reusable validation pipeline and a resource approval, then explain exactly what to preview and how to prove a developer cannot bypass it.
assertions: Separates the reusable/versioned template, branch build-validation policy, and protected-resource approval/check as distinct native controls
Binds validation and evidence to the exact pull-request source commit and preserves native policy, build, check/approval, and artifact references
Requires discover, exact preview, authorization, idempotent apply, authoritative re-read, positive and bypass-negative probes, rollback, and drift detection

evals.prompt: A script written for Azure DevOps Services REST 7.2 needs to run against Azure DevOps Server. Can it silently retry with an older api-version when a field is rejected?
assertions: Requires explicit Services versus Server release detection and a version-pinned capability result
Rejects silent API downgrade or weaker fallback and returns unsupported/unknown when the Server probe has not passed
Distinguishes documentation conformance from a live Server conformance pass

evals.prompt: Onboard Azure Pipelines to deploy through an Azure service connection. We want no stored client secret, minimum permissions, expiry verification, drift detection, and complete uninstall guidance.
assertions: Prefers workload identity federation or managed identity and does not create a long-lived secret by default
Previews issuer/audience/subject, project/pipeline authorization, Azure role scope, credential/network/data changes, and rollback without exposing credential values
Verifies temporary credential expiry, an allowed action, an out-of-scope denial, authoritative service-connection/RBAC state, drift, and owned-resource-only rollback

evals.prompt: Open a pull request on Azure DevOps Services from the shell for branch feat/x against main, and give me the URL and a mergeability check.
assertions: Pushes the branch first and derives --org/--project/--repository from the git remote (v3/<org>/<project>/<repo>), not the configured CLI default
Runs az repos pr create, captures pullRequestId with --query pullRequestId -o tsv, and builds the .../_git/<repo>/pullrequest/<id> URL
Confirms mergeStatus is succeeded via az repos pr show and notes --draft true for work in progress

evals.prompt: I have to use a personal access token for an Azure DevOps CLI flow that cannot use az login. How do I scope, store, and hand it to the tooling safely?
assertions: Scopes the PAT to only Code (Read & Write) and Work Items (Read & Write), a single org, and the shortest expiry, created/rotated at _usersSettings/tokens
Stores it in the OS keychain or a secret manager and reads it into AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT at call time (Basic :PAT for raw REST), never inlining, echoing, or committing the value
Verifies the credential with a cheap pre-call HTTP probe and treats a 203/HTML sign-in redirect as an unauthenticated token rather than success
